## Teaching points

1. Focal bony pain after a jump in training load suggests a stress injury. Early films can be normal.
2. Gradual focal pain with a rapid training increase suggests bone stress injury, even without a single traumatic event.
3. Assess energy intake, menstrual changes and bone-health risks as well as protecting the painful foot.
4. The radiograph shows a shaft stress fracture here; a negative early film would not exclude the diagnosis.
